messages.subject: CamtrapR reads the image metadata - can I do the reverse? I.e. write to the image.
messages.subject_clean: CamtrapR reads the image metadata - can I do the reverse? I.e. write to the image.
messages.body_plain:
Jürgen

At the moment I use ExifPro to add metadata (species and station) to the image which I then read into camtrapR.  I am really grateful for that successful workflow.

But I am wondering if I can use camtrapR (and its use of ExifTools) to write back additional (or corrected metadata) to the original image? I like the idea of the image, the source data, containing the attributes.  Can I write an R function (in camptrapR so I benefit from camtrapR's use of ExifTools) that will do this?

David

messages.subject: Re: SDH Date Range Error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,
I cannot reproduce the same error, but there's a few other issues here and I got a capthist object at the end. When loading the tables I found that the record table csv has columns separeted by semicolon, the other two csv have commas.

Running your code as is I get:
Error in spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableInd,  :
  there is a mismatch between station IDs in CTtable and rownames in camOp
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In `!=.default`(CTtable[, stationCol], rownames(camOp)) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
2: In is.na <http://is.na>(e1) | is.na <http://is.na>(e2) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

Problem here is that the camera Operation matrix has 30 rows, the camera trap table has 67 (because there is several camera per station. I removed the duplicates with:

ct_info_table2 <- ct_info_table[!duplicated(ct_info_table$Station),]

This is just a quick and dirty fix, please check thoroughly.

Then, I got this:

Error in spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableInd,  :
  at least 1 entry in recordDateTimeCol of recordTableIndividual could not be interpreted using recordDateTimeFormat
In addition: Warning message:
timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC

Meaning the date/time format is wrong (it is 2013-02-17 00:29, without seconds, most likely due to Excel).
Either you change argument recordDateTimeFormat or restore the original from the Date and Time column (with paste()). I took the first apprioach here.

Ultimately, I used:

  SDH <- spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableInd,

                                 species               = "Hyaena_Spotted_2013_Images",

                                 output                = "binary",
                                 camOp                 = camOPTMatrix,

                                 CTtable               = ct_info_table2,

                                 stationCol            = "Station",
                                 speciesCol            = "Species",
                                 Xcol                  = "utm_x",
                                 Ycol                  = "utm_y",
                                 individualCol         = "Individual",
                                 recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",

                                 recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M",

                                 occasionLength        = 1,
                                 day1                  = "survey",

                                 occasionStartTime     = 0,
                                 includeEffort         = TRUE,
                                 makeRMarkInput        = FALSE
  )

and only got warnings:

Warning messages:
1: timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC
2: record date after camera operation date range:  Station4
3: 1 records out of 223 were removed because they were taken after the end of the last occasion
Station4: 2013-04-02 00:43:00

> summary(SDH)
Object class       capthist
Detector type      proximity
Detector number    30
Average spacing    3142.735 m
x-range            379440.9 411743.9 m
y-range            6867394 6893572 m

etc etc.

-----------
Here's the entire code:

library(camtrapR)

wd <- "..."    # set the directory containing the tables

setwd(wd)

ct_info_table <- read.csv("ct_info_table.csv", row.names = 1, sep = ",")
camOPTMatrix <- read.csv("camOPTMatrix.csv", row.names = 1, sep = ",", check.names = FALSE)
recordTableInd <- read.csv("recordTableInd.csv", sep = ";")      # note the semicolon separator here

ct_info_table2 <- ct_info_table[!duplicated(ct_info_table$Station),]

SDH <- spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableInd,

                               species               = "Hyaena_Spotted_2013_Images",

                               output                = "binary",
                               camOp                 = camOPTMatrix,

                               CTtable               = ct_info_table2,

                               stationCol            = "Station",
                               speciesCol            = "Species",
                               Xcol                  = "utm_x",
                               Ycol                  = "utm_y",
                               individualCol         = "Individual",
                               recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",

                               recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M",

                               occasionLength        = 1,
                               day1                  = "survey",

                               occasionStartTime     = 0,
                               includeEffort         = TRUE,
                               makeRMarkInput        = FALSE
)

Best,
Jürgen

messages.body_plain:
Hi Inés,
this is not implemented in the package. You could probably write some simple code in R to achieve this, like:

subset record table to species of interest
create a matrix with all unique stations (or cameras) as rows and all image filenames as columns, all values are NA. (it will be a very big matrix!)
Based on the record table, find all images at a given station (or camera), write value 1 to the corresponding matrix cells.
repeat for all stations

Just wondering, what kind of analysis would you use that data format for?
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Can't Generate Suvery Report
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bazilah,
it seems that there is a mismatch between the station IDs in your camera trap table and the station IDs in the record table.

See this post <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/camtrapr/unique%7Csort:date/camtrapr/kLAzF-CfiW4/Brx8690aAQAJ> and the code there:

# show all unique entries of the record table station column that are not in the camera trap station table
unique(rec.table60$Station)[!unique(rec.table60$Station) %in% cams$Station]

# show all unique entries of the camera trap station table station column that are not in record table
unique(cams$Station)[!unique(cams$Station) %in% unique(rec.table60$Station)]

If these lines returns station IDs that are not matched, correct them, then rerun your code.
If that does not help, please let us know.
Best,
Jürgen
